strengths: Addresses an important and timely problem: watermarking 3DGS models while supporting compression, with clear practical significance for commercial deployment

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Blender, LLFF, Mip-NeRF 360), compression methods (HAC, ContextGS), distortion types, and bit-lengths, with significant improvements over baselines (95.92% vs 46.52% post-compression bit accuracy)
Quantization distortion layer is an elegant and intuitive solution for making watermarks robust to quantization through pre-adaptation during training

Thoughtful design choices that preserve structural consistency: embedding in anchor features rather than direct parameters, using DWT for low-frequency watermark embedding, HSV loss for perceptual color alignment
Solid ablation studies demonstrating the necessity of each component (FAG, HSV loss, frequency loss, and QDL)
Clear and generally well-written presentation with informative figures, particularly the system overview in Figure 2
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: the learnable embedding feature (Eq. 5) is straightforward, quantization distortion applies standard techniques to this domain, and frequency-aware anchor growing combines existing methods. Primarily an engineering contribution rather than conceptual innovation

Reliance on pre-trained HiDDeN decoder requiring separate training for each bit-length, with decoder frozen during watermark training, limiting flexibility and adaptability—inadequately addressed despite being mentioned as a limitation

Critical design choices lack rigorous justification: why tanh specifically (Eq. 5) vs clipping? Why embed in low-frequency for 3DGS? Why these specific hyperparameter values (τ=0.3, β, λ parameters)? No sensitivity analysis provided

Reproducibility concerns: many implementation details relegated to supplementary material; complex multi-component system with numerous hyperparameters; unclear training procedures and convergence criteria; frequency-aware anchor growing involves many steps with limited algorithmic clarity

Suspicious baseline results: GaussianMarker shows PSNR of 6.26 in Figure 3 (extremely poor); large unexplained post-compression drops for some methods suggest baselines may not be properly configured for anchor-based compression framework

Weak theoretical justification: lacks formal explanation of why quantization noise injection preserves watermarks; no information-theoretic analysis; connection between low-frequency embedding and compression robustness not rigorously established

Incomplete evaluation: no comparison with post-training quantization-aware fine-tuning; limited analysis of watermark-quality trade-offs; no evaluation on very large-scale scenes; training overhead not discussed; no assessment of adversarial watermark removal attempts beyond simple distortions

Circular baseline comparison: claiming to be 'first to embed watermarks in anchor-based 3DGS' when baselines weren't designed for this framework; WateRF and GaussianMarker are NeRF/non-anchor methods, making comparisons potentially unfair

Limited security discussion: assumes honest watermark extraction; low-frequency embedding is a known attack surface without adequate discussion; no comparison with robust watermarking literature from other domains

Clarity issues in technical exposition: Section 4.3 on frequency-aware anchor growing is dense and difficult to follow; assumes center regions are low-frequency without justification; notation inconsistencies (f, f', f^w); missing implementation details for critical components (MLP architectures)

strengths: Addresses a genuine and important practical gap: first method to successfully combine watermarking with anchor-based 3DGS compression, where existing methods completely fail (95.92% vs 46.52% bit accuracy after compression)
Strong and comprehensive experimental evaluation across three datasets with robustness testing against multiple image and model distortions, showing dramatic improvements over baselines

Well-engineered technical approach that thoughtfully combines established techniques: learnable watermark embedding maintains structural consistency, quantization distortion layer enables compression robustness, frequency-aware anchor growing preserves details
Clear presentation with good visualizations, reproducible implementation details, and thorough ablation studies demonstrating the contribution of each component
Practical significance: solves a real problem for real-world deployment of 3DGS models requiring both watermarking and compression
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual technical components: QDL is standard noise injection, frequency-aware anchor growing combines existing methods, watermark embedding is a straightforward learnable perturbation with tanh constraint
Narrow scope restricted to anchor-based 3DGS methods; unclear generalization to other 3DGS variants or 3D representations, limiting broader impact
Dependence on pre-trained HiDDeN decoder (one per bit-length) adds practical setup requirement and makes the approach less self-contained

Insufficient security and adversarial analysis: no formal security model, no evaluation against adversarial attacks designed to remove watermarks, model distortion tests are limited to simple perturbations

Incomplete technical justification: Eq. 6 allows learnable quantization step to potentially minimize quantization effect (though not observed empirically); high-frequency mask creation seems ad-hoc; limited sensitivity analysis for multiple hyperparameters
Missing comparisons: no explicit baseline of naive watermarking followed by compression to quantify QDL benefit; modest improvement from frequency-aware anchor growing in ablation (94.68% → 95.16%)
Limited theoretical analysis: why QDL works lacks formal justification, no guarantees on watermark survival, no analysis of error patterns in watermark extraction
Narrow evaluation scope: only tested with single A6000 GPU, standard scene sizes, no analysis of scalability to very large models or computational overhead

strengths: Addresses a genuine, previously unexplored problem: watermark robustness to 3DGS compression, which is practically important for deployed models
Comprehensive experimental validation across 25 scenes with thorough comparisons to four baselines and extensive ablation studies
Strong empirical results maintaining ~95% bit accuracy before and after compression while preserving high rendering quality (PSNR ~27.65)
Sound technical approach appropriately combining quantization distortion layer, frequency-aware anchor growing, and HSV loss for the compression-robustness problem
Excellent presentation with clear writing, well-designed figures, and thorough supplementary materials with implementation details
Maintains real-time rendering performance (>30 FPS) while adding watermarking functionality
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (quantization noise injection, frequency analysis, HSV color space) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Scope restricted to anchor-based 3DGS (Scaffold-GS), limiting applicability to vanilla 3DGS and reducing broader impact on the community
Pre-trained decoder dependency requiring separate HiDDeN training for each message length adds practical deployment complexity not fully addressed
Insufficient security analysis for a watermarking paper: limited adversarial attacks tested, no theoretical imperceptibility bounds or removal attack discussion
Ad-hoc design choices lack rigorous justification: radial-distance high-pass filter, median±epsilon threshold selection, multiple hyperparameters without sensitivity analysis
Unfair baseline comparisons: GuardSplat required significant modification to use anchor features instead of SH coefficients, potentially misrepresenting its capability
Missing statistical analysis: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing; variance across scenes not characterized
Computational overhead during watermark embedding not analyzed: training time, memory cost, and QDL efficiency not discussed
Limited compression evaluation: only two compression schemes tested; generalization to other quantization approaches unclear
Insufficient watermark security discussion: no capacity bounds, information-theoretic analysis, or investigation of watermark removal attacks
